grh_9f394783b5da5f43fc64.title: The Shooting of Wyatt King
paragraphs: After robbing the Copper Springs bank, outlaw Wyatt King is found badly wounded and insists that Britt was the man who outdrew him. Britt has never met King, but Wyatt privately admits that he would rather lose to the famous Six Shooter than confess that an ordinary gray-haired bank teller shot him while defending a horse. Britt identifies teller Jonas Pilgrim as the real gunman, though Jonas is equally eager to avoid the story because of his domineering wife's rules. When Wyatt later escapes and Britt returns him to jail, Britt arranges for Jonas to be sitting watch when the posse comes back, leaving the town convinced that the unassuming teller single-handedly recaptured the outlaw.

grh_9fc3f1d828439b1d137d.title: The Affairs of Susan
paragraphs: Susan's prospective husband tries to understand the woman he plans to marry by questioning the men who knew her before him. Ex-husband Roger remembers an innocent country girl, writer Bill recalls an intellectual companion, and Westerner Mike describes an adventurous outdoor woman, leaving the fiancé wondering which Susan is real. The answer is that each man saw the side of her that his own expectations brought out. After the newer suitors step aside, Roger returns and admits that he was too impatient to understand the young woman he married. Susan realizes she still loves him, and the divorced couple reunites.
